## management-group-parents

Sprint 10 step 7 (2026-10-09) made `Get-OERManagementGroup` show the parent of every LISTED
management group, and made `-Expand` and `-Recurse` need `-Name`. In 1.1.3 a listed group's
`ParentId`, `ParentName` and `ParentDisplayName` came out empty, since the list answer carries no
parent (Learn: a Management Groups - List item has `id`, `name`, `type`, `properties.displayName`
and `properties.tenantId` only), so an empty parent could not be told apart from "this group has no
parent". And `-Expand` or `-Recurse` without `-Name` was silently ignored: the command listed the
groups, without children.

**The measurement (2026-10-09, reads only; counts and True/False only).** Two app-only identities
in the test tenant: the live-verification identity (Owner on one subscription, no role on any
management group) and a second identity with no Azure role at all.

- MEASURED, the live-verification identity: Management Groups - List, at api-version `2020-05-01`
  and at `2023-04-01`, answers `403 AuthorizationFailed` (action
  `Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/read` over `/providers/Microsoft.Management`). A caller
  that can read no group is refused, not answered with an empty list.
- MEASURED, the same identity: Entities - List
  (`POST /providers/Microsoft.Management/getEntities?api-version=2020-05-01`, no body, sent through
  the module's own `Invoke-OERArmRequest`) answers `200` with 3 entities: 1 subscription and 2
  management groups (the tenant root group and one more), both groups with `permissions`
  `noaccess`. The non-root group carries `parent.id`, `parentNameChain` and
  `parentDisplayNameChain`: True. The last element of `parentNameChain` equals the last segment of
  `parent.id`: True (1 of 1). The root group, whose `name` equals the tenant id, has no parent:
  True. The subscription carries `parent.id`: True. With `&$view=GroupsOnly` the answer holds 2
  entities, the groups only.
- MEASURED, the same identity: on the tenant root group, a plain GET, a GET with
  `$expand=children&$recurse=true` and a `/descendants` read each answer `403 AuthorizationFailed`.
  A GET of either management group (plain, `$expand=children`, `$expand=path`) answers `403`; both
  are `noaccess`.
- MEASURED, the identity with no Azure role: the list answers `403`, Entities - List answers `200`
  with 0 entities, and the root group's reads answer `403`.
- Learn ("Azure permissions for Management and governance"): the list and a group read need
  `Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/read`, `/descendants` needs
  `Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/descendants/read`, and Entities - List is the action
  `Microsoft.Management/getEntities/action` -- which, by the role-less identity's `200`, needs no
  role assignment of its own. Learn (Entities - List): `parentNameChain` and
  `parentDisplayNameChain` run from the root group to the immediate parent. Learn (Management
  Groups - Get): a group read carries `properties.details.parent` (`id`, `name`, `displayName`),
  which the `-Name` path reads through `ConvertTo-OERManagementGroup`. Learn (management groups
  overview): the root management group's id is the tenant id.

**What the measurement does not show.** The live-verification identity's list was refused, so the
parent read was never measured on a LISTED group, and no answer held a group more than one level
below the root. That the answer is mapped to the right parent on several levels (three, in mocked
answers) is proved by unit tests (`tests/Unit/Private/Get-OERManagementGroupParent.Tests.ps1` and
the Context `the parent of every listed group (A10)` in
`tests/Unit/Public/Get-OERManagementGroup.Tests.ps1`) and is left for the operator to confirm in a
tenant where the groups can be listed. Not verified
live either: an Entities - List answer of more than one page (the test tenant's is one page; see
the paging bullet under [#arm-transport](#arm-transport)), and anything about caching or delay in
Entities - List. The list's own delay for a new group stays as
[#inventory-azure-eligibility](#inventory-azure-eligibility) records it.

**Why Entities - List, once per list.** It gives the parent of every group the caller can reach in
one call, and needs no role of its own. The alternatives:

- The root group with `$expand=children&$recurse=true`, or the root's `/descendants`, would walk
  the tree in one call as well, but both need read on the ROOT group -- measured `403` without it --
  so a caller with Reader on a subtree only would lose every parent. The same measurement
  confirms, for an identity without read on the root, the reason given under
  [#inventory-azure-eligibility](#inventory-azure-eligibility) for not enumerating from the root.
- A GET per listed group reads `properties.details.parent`, as `-Name` does, but costs one call per
  group.

If a tenant ever shows Entities - List missing or mis-stating a group that the list returns, the
fallback is that GET per group; until then, such a group keeps an empty parent and is reported
(below), so it is not left silently empty.

**How the answer is read.** `Get-OERManagementGroupParent`, the single owner of the call, keys its
map on the entity's `name` (case-insensitive) and takes an entity only when its `type` is
`Microsoft.Management/managementGroups`, its `parent.id` is a string that is not blank and whose
last segment is not blank, its `parentNameChain` has at least one element and ends in that same last
segment (compared case-insensitively), and its `parentDisplayNameChain` ends in an element that is
not blank. `ParentId` is `parent.id`, `ParentName` the last segment of `parent.id`, and
`ParentDisplayName` the last element of `parentDisplayNameChain`. The `parentNameChain` condition is
there because the display name comes from a chain and not from `parent.id`: an answer whose chains
end in another group than the one `parent.id` names would otherwise put that other group's display
name beside the right `ParentId` and `ParentName`. Learn's own Entities - List sample is such an
answer -- its `parent.id` names the tenant root group while both chains end in another group -- and
the measured equality above is 1 of 1, for a group directly under the root. The condition compares
the name chain only, so a `parentDisplayNameChain` that disagrees with its own `parentNameChain` is
not caught. Any other entity is left out, so a group the answer misses or mis-states is reported as
unread. `Get-OERManagementGroup` sends the call only when the list holds a group other than the
tenant root group, and only after the list itself succeeded.

**A parent that cannot be read is reported, not left silently empty.** An empty `ParentId` reads as
"this group has no parent". So a listed group whose parent was not read -- the Entities - List call
failed, or its answer has no usable parent for that group -- is still written, with its three parent
properties empty, and after EVERY group has been written the command writes ONE non-terminating
error for the whole list: `ManagementGroupParentReadFailed`, category `ReadError`, its target object
the unread groups' names as a `[string[]]`. Its message, when the answer had no parent for two
groups:

```text
Could not read the parent of 2 management group(s): 'mg-a', 'mg-b' -- the entity listing (Entities - List) returned no usable parent for them. Their ParentId, ParentName and ParentDisplayName are empty, which here does not mean that they have no parent.
```

When the call itself failed, the reason reads `the entity listing failed: ` followed by that call's
own message with its trailing full stops trimmed (the sentence adds its own), and the failed call's
exception is the record's `InnerException`. Every group is written to the pipeline before the
error, so a caller that consumes the pipeline (`| ForEach-Object { ... }`) sees every group. Under
`-ErrorAction Stop`, or a global `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`, an assignment of the whole
result (`$Groups = Get-OERManagementGroup`, with or without `@(...)`) receives none, since the
error ends the statement. That is measured on a plain stand-in function that writes three objects
and then one non-terminating error through `$PSCmdlet.WriteError`, as `Write-CmdletError` does
(2026-10-09): each of the three assignments leaves the variable as it was, and a `ForEach-Object`
consumer sees all three objects, under `-ErrorAction Stop` and under the global preference alike.
It follows the rule behind `Get-OERGroup`'s `GroupMemberReadFailed` (see
[#typed-group-member-read](#typed-group-member-read)): a value that could not be read is reported
as unread, not left silently empty. `Get-OERGroup` omits the property; here the three parent
properties stay on the object, empty, and the error says that they are. A failed LIST is reported
as before, as its own error (`AuthorizationFailed` for a caller that can read no group), and no
parent read follows.

**The tenant root group is recognised, not looked up.** A listed item whose `name` equals its
`properties.tenantId` -- compared case-insensitively, and never for a blank name -- is the tenant
root group (Learn: its id is the tenant id; measured: the root entity's name equals the tenant id
and it has no parent). Its parent properties stay empty with no error, and when it is the only group
listed, no Entities - List call is sent. A root that came back under another name, or without a
`tenantId`, would be named in `ManagementGroupParentReadFailed` -- visible, never silent.

**The export never reads the parents.** `Resolve-OERInventoryScopeTree` lists the full tree through
the private `Get-OERManagementGroupList` -- the list call `Get-OERManagementGroup` makes -- and
converts the items itself with `ConvertTo-OERManagementGroup`; it never calls
`Get-OERManagementGroup` without `-Name`. A failed or refused Entities - List call therefore cannot
make an export partial or add to its `SkippedScopes`, and the bundle needs no parent: the
`scopeHierarchy.json` management group nodes carry `name`, `displayName` and `id` only. Its
`-ManagementGroup` branch still calls `Get-OERManagementGroup -Name ... -ErrorAction Stop`, which
reads one group by name and sends no Entities - List call.

**`Get-OERManagementGroupList` is the single owner of the Management Groups - List call (Sprint 11
step 12, BL-120 point 1).** In Sprint 10 step 7 it was not: `Resolve-OERScope`'s display-name
fallback, which the RBAC and PIM cmdlets reach through `-ManagementGroup`, sent its own list call, and
nothing held the two together beyond the api-version documentation gate in
`tests/QA/sourcehygiene.tests.ps1`, which checks that each version is documented, not that the two
calls agree. The fallback now reads the list through `Get-OERManagementGroupList` and matches
`properties.displayName` on the raw items it returns, as before; a failed listing throws from the
helper as the wrapper did there, and never reads as "not found". The helper has three callers:
`Get-OERManagementGroup`, `Resolve-OERInventoryScopeTree` and `Resolve-OERScope`. The Entities - List
call keeps its own owner, `Get-OERManagementGroupParent`.

**`-Expand` and `-Recurse` need `-Name`, refused at binding.** The parameters sit in two parameter
sets: `List`, the default, and `ByName`, to which `-Expand` and `-Recurse` belong and in which
`-Name` is mandatory at position 0; `-TenantId` is at position 1 in every set and keeps
`[ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]`. A call with `-Expand` or `-Recurse` and no `-Name` can bind only
`ByName`, whose mandatory `-Name` is missing. What happens then depends on whether the host can
prompt. MEASURED on a plain stand-in function with the same param block (2026-10-09): where it
cannot -- a host-less runspace, `pwsh -NonInteractive`, `pwsh -File` with stdin redirected from an
empty file, and a `Start-ThreadJob` job -- the call fails with `MissingMandatoryParameter`; where it
can, PowerShell asks for `-Name` instead: an interactive console prompts, and a `Start-Job` job is
blocked, waiting for input. A real CI runner was not measured. The refusal comes before `begin`
runs, so nothing is signed in or sent, for a call with no pipeline input; in a pipeline `-Name`
binds per object, so `begin` signs in first and an object without a name fails
`InputObjectNotBound`, as in 1.1.3.

Also measured on that stand-in: parameter sets drop PowerShell's automatic positions -- `X mg1`
failed with `PositionalParameterNotFound` -- so `Position = 0` and `Position = 1` are declared
explicitly, which restores 1.1.3's positional binding exactly (`X mg1`, `X mg1 t1`); `-Recurse`,
`-Expand`, `-Expand -Recurse` and `-TenantId t -Recurse` without `-Name` fail with
`MissingMandatoryParameter` in a host-less runspace; and piped objects carrying
`ManagementGroupName`, `ManagementGroup` or `Name` bind `-Name` as before, while an object with
none of them fails `InputObjectNotBound`, as before. The unit tests prove the refusals in a fresh
host-less runspace (the Context `parameter sets (A10)` in
`tests/Unit/Public/Get-OERManagementGroup.Tests.ps1`), never in the Pester host itself, where a
missing mandatory parameter can prompt.

**An empty name is refused, not read as the list.** A mandatory `[string]` parameter refuses an
empty string at binding, so `-Name ''` and a piped empty `ManagementGroupName` now fail with
`ParameterArgumentValidationErrorEmptyStringNotAllowed`. In 1.1.3 both fell through `if ($Name)` to
the list branch and listed every group. An empty name was never a request for the list, so the
refusal stays. Do not add `[AllowEmptyString()]` to bring the old behaviour back: the process block
now branches on the parameter set, not on `$Name`, so an empty name would be sent as a name.

### CLAUDE.md text for management-group-parents

What CLAUDE.md said about this rule before Sprint 11 step 11b cut it to the rule itself:

**`Get-OERManagementGroupParent` is the single owner of the Entities - List call**
(`POST /providers/Microsoft.Management/getEntities`, api-version `2020-05-01`, `$view=GroupsOnly`,
`-All`), which `Get-OERManagementGroup` sends at most once per list to fill the parent of every
listed group, since the Management Groups - List answer carries none. The inventory walk
(`Resolve-OERInventoryScopeTree`) lists management groups through `Get-OERManagementGroupList`,
converts them itself and never calls `Get-OERManagementGroup` without `-Name`, so the parent read
can never add a failure mode to an export. `Get-OERManagementGroupList` is NOT the single owner of
the list call -- `Resolve-OERScope` still sends its own -- so never describe it as one.
`Why: docs/development/rationale.md#management-group-parents`

(Superseded by Sprint 11 step 12: `Get-OERManagementGroupList` IS now the single owner of the
Management Groups - List call and `Resolve-OERScope` calls it; see above.)

## lighthouse-delegations

Sprint 11 step 6b (BL-133) made `Export-OERInventory` read the Azure Lighthouse delegations at the
subscriptions its Azure walk visits and write them to `lighthouseDelegations.json`, as read-only
context and a finding. This anchor records the problem, the measurement, the rulings with what each
costs if it is wrong, the known limits and the mutation proofs. `Get-OERInventoryLighthouseDelegation`
is the single owner of the read, and `ConvertTo-OERLighthouseDelegation` of the row. No ErrorId, no
public parameter and no property of the `Omnicit.EntraRBAC.InventoryBundle` object was added, and
`inventory.json` keeps its shape and content. The pinned api-version is listed under
[#arm-transport](#arm-transport).

**The problem.** Azure Lighthouse lets a managing tenant, a service provider for example, manage
subscriptions or resource groups of a customer tenant: a registration definition (the offer, the
managing tenant and its authorizations) and a registration assignment in each delegated scope give
principals of the managing tenant Azure built-in roles over that scope. Microsoft Learn states that
the customer does not see that access where it lists role assignments: "View and manage service
providers" says that, in the Azure portal or through the APIs, "customers can't see role assignments
for users from the service provider tenant who have access through Azure Lighthouse", and
"Cross-tenant management experiences", under its current limitations, that such assignments are
visible only in the Delegations section of Azure Lighthouse or through the Azure Lighthouse API. So
an export that read only role assignments showed none of that access, and nothing in the bundle said
that another tenant held any.

**The measurement (2026-10-15, reads only).** Two app-only identities in the test tenant: the
live-verification identity (a role on one subscription) and a second identity with no Azure role.
No tenant value is recorded here.

- MEASURED, the live-verification identity, on the test subscription: the registration assignment
  list, at api-version `2022-10-01`, with `$expandRegistrationDefinition=true` and without it,
  answers `200` with an empty `value`; the registration definition list answers `200` with an empty
  `value`. The resource provider `Microsoft.ManagedServices` is `NotRegistered` on that subscription,
  and both lists still answer `200` with an empty list, so an unregistered provider does not fail
  the read. One resource group's assignment list answers `200` with an empty list.
- MEASURED, the same identity: a registration definition list read at a resource group answers
  `InvalidRegistrationDefinitionUri` ("Registration definitions are allowed at subscription scope
  only"), so the definitions are read only at the subscription. An assignment list read at a
  resource group that does not exist answers `200` with an empty list, so a named resource group is
  read without a check that it exists, and an absent one is a group with nothing delegated, not a
  failed read.
- MEASURED, the same identity: a role definition read by a built-in role GUID at the subscription
  (`roleDefinitions/{guid}`, api-version `2022-04-01`) answers `200` with `properties.roleName`; an
  unknown GUID answers `RoleDefinitionDoesNotExist`.
- MEASURED, the identity with no Azure role: both lists answer `403 AuthorizationFailed`, naming the
  actions `Microsoft.ManagedServices/registrationAssignments/read` and
  `Microsoft.ManagedServices/registrationDefinitions/read`, which Reader's `*/read` covers; its
  subscription list answers `200` with no subscription.
- DOCUMENTED (Microsoft Learn, Registration Assignments - List and Registration Definitions - List):
  api-version `2022-10-01`, `GET {scope}/providers/Microsoft.ManagedServices/registrationAssignments`
  with the optional `$expandRegistrationDefinition=true` and
  `GET {scope}/providers/Microsoft.ManagedServices/registrationDefinitions`, both paged with
  `nextLink`. An authorization carries `principalId`, `principalIdDisplayName`, `roleDefinitionId` (a
  built-in role GUID) and, for User Access Administrator, `delegatedRoleDefinitionIds`; an eligible
  authorization carries the same and a `justInTimeAccessPolicy`. The definition carries
  `registrationDefinitionName` (the offer), `managedByTenantId`, `managedByTenantName` and
  `description`.
- DOCUMENTED (Microsoft Learn, Azure Lighthouse architecture): a registration definition is created
  at the subscription for each delegated subscription, or in each subscription that holds a
  delegated resource group, and a registration assignment in each delegated scope. Learn does NOT
  say whether a subscription's assignment list also returns the assignments of its resource groups.
- NOT MEASURED: a tenant that holds a delegation. Every list answered empty, so the row shape rests
  on the documented fields and on mocked answers (known limit (b)).

**How the read works.** The reader's help is the reference; in short, it groups the walk's scopes per
subscription, letter case ignored, and skips a scope that is not under `/subscriptions/` with no
request. Per subscription it reads the two paged lists. A subscription the walk names whole whose
definitions are not all named by an assignment of its own list also gets one resource group listing
(api-version `2025-04-01`) and the assignment list of every group; a subscription named only through
a scope below it gets the assignment list of each resource group it names. An assignment's
definition is the one the list expanded, or else the listed definition it names; an assignment with
neither makes the subscription unread. Assignments are deduplicated on their id (a blank id on scope
and definition id), a subscription named only through a scope below it keeps the delegations at
the subscription and at the named groups, and a subscription's rows join the result only when every
read of it succeeded. Then each distinct role GUID is read once, at the subscription of the first
row that carries it, and the rows are sorted by scope, managing tenant, offer and assignment id. A
failed subscription names each of its scopes in `Unread` as `lighthouseDelegations at <scope>`, adds
one cause and writes one warning; a failed role read, other than a role that does not exist, names
`lighthouseDelegations role <guid>` the same way. Both catches scrub the error record first, and the
reader writes no error record.

**R-1 (the api-version).** `2022-10-01` for both Microsoft.ManagedServices lists, read at every
subscription the walk visits: the latest GA version Learn documents for List, and measured `200` on
the test subscription. Cost if wrong (a later GA version changes the shape): the converter reads only
documented fields, and a version bump is one constant plus the line under
[#arm-transport](#arm-transport).

**R-2 (two reads per subscription, and the fallback).** The assignments with
`$expandRegistrationDefinition=true`, and the definitions; a definition that no assignment of the
subscription list references triggers one resource group listing and one assignment read per
resource group. Learn places every delegation's definition at its subscription but does not say
whether the subscription list returns resource group assignments, so this finds a resource group
delegation either way. Cost if wrong (the subscription list does return them): the fallback then
fires only for a definition with no assignment at all, at the cost of one listing plus one read per
group in such a subscription.

**R-3 (always on).** The read is always on when an Azure section is included, and the file is
absent otherwise, like `azurePimEligibility.json`; there is no switch and no `-Include` value (A9
not used). Two extra paged reads per subscription are small beside the walk's existing per-scope
reads, and a switch would hide another tenant's access by default. Cost if wrong: A9 still allows a
switch in a later step.

**R-4 (a failed read is named).** In `IncompleteReads`, not `SkippedScopes`, whose documented meaning
is `roleAssignments.json` and `roleManagementPolicies.json`; appended last, as
`lighthouseDelegations at <scope>`; a subscription is read whole or not at all. Cost if wrong: the
entries move with one line, and the partial clause and the README label follow the prefix.

**R-5 (role names).** One GET per distinct role GUID at a subscription. `RoleDefinitionDoesNotExist`
or `NotFound` leaves `roleName` null and is not unread; any other failure leaves it null and is named
`lighthouseDelegations role <guid>`. This is the existing role name lookup pattern
(`Get-OERRoleAssignment`), plus the rule that a failed read is named. Cost if wrong: a failed name
lookup could be left unnamed, at the cost of an unexplained null.

**R-6 (eligible authorizations).** `eligibleAuthorizations` (just-in-time) are written beside
`authorizations`, and an authorization keeps `delegatedRoleDefinitionIds`: both are access another
tenant holds, and the specification's "every authorization" covers them. Cost if wrong: two keys
come out of the converter.

**R-7 (one warning).** One warning when delegations were read, before the bundle's `ShouldProcess`,
as for the export's other findings. Cost if wrong: one `Write-Warning` is deleted.

**R-8 (no new output property).** No property is added to the `InventoryBundle` object; the count is
the file's. Cost if wrong: an added property is a later, separate decision.

**R-9 (a scope below a subscription).** A `-Scope` below a subscription reads its subscription's two
lists and its resource group's assignment list, and keeps the delegations at the subscription and at
that resource group, the ones that cover it; a management group or the root scope reads nothing.
Cost if wrong: the filter is one predicate.

**R-10 (a level that could not be listed).** A failed scope enumeration names
`lighthouseDelegations at <all Azure scopes: scope enumeration failed>` and a failed subscription
listing `lighthouseDelegations at <subscriptions: the listing failed>`; a failed management group
listing adds nothing, since no delegation is made at a management group and the subscriptions are
listed apart. Cost if wrong: one more mapping line.

**R-11 (two guards kept as equivalent mutants).** `Export-OERInventory` keeps
`if ($null -ne $LighthouseRead)` and `if ($null -ne $LighthouseCause)`, which no test can turn red
(see the equivalent mutants below): they make the null case explicit at no cost. Cost if wrong: two
lines come out.

**R-12 (the direction of a delegation).** The whole-branch review found that a delegation can run
the other way. Microsoft Learn ("Cross-tenant management experiences") states that the
`HomeTenantId` and `ManagedByTenantIds` of each subscription Azure PowerShell returns "help you
identify whether a returned subscription belongs to a managed tenant or to your managing tenant",
and that the REST API's Subscriptions - Get and Subscriptions - List include `ManagedByTenant`: in a
managing (service provider) tenant the subscription list also returns the customer subscriptions
delegated to it (inferred from Learn, not measured here). The export's walk then visits them, and
the Lighthouse read can return a row whose `managedByTenantId` is THIS tenant: access this tenant
holds over another tenant's subscription, while every text described each row as another tenant's
access here. The ruling fixes it in the texts and the bundle README, not by filtering subscriptions
by tenant: the walk's scopes stay what they are for every Azure file, so the Lighthouse read covers
what the role assignment read covers, and a row's direction is decidable from its
`managedByTenantId` against the `tenantId` of `inventory.json` (the Graph token's tenant, which
`Export-OERInventory` already holds as `$DocumentTenantId`). The warning named no direction;
`Get-OERInventoryReadme -TenantId` (optional; `Export-OERInventory` passed `$DocumentTenantId`)
marked a bullet whose `managedByTenantId` equalled it, letter case ignored and never when the tenant
was blank, as access this tenant holds over another tenant's subscription or resource group; and the
export help, the prompt, README.md, the about topic and `docs/inventory-to-llm/README.md` said so in
one sentence each. Cost if wrong (the architect prefers this tenant's own subscriptions only):
carrying each subscription's tenant through the scope tree and skipping the foreign ones is a later
step. The reads from a managing tenant are unmeasured (known limit (g)), so the sprint's C-check
records it.

*What BL-150 changed (Sprint 11 step 6c, decision A19).* The architect took the later step R-12
named: the export's Azure walk no longer reaches a subscription another tenant delegated to this
one. `Get-OERSubscriptionHomeTenant` keeps every listed subscription whose home tenant (ARM's
subscription `tenantId`) is not the tenant of the session's Microsoft Graph token out of the walk,
so the Lighthouse read is never made at such a subscription
([#home-tenant-subscriptions](#home-tenant-subscriptions)). The mark is removed with it (that step's
Ruling R-9): `Get-OERInventoryReadme` no longer takes `-TenantId`, `Export-OERInventory` no longer
passes `$DocumentTenantId` to it, and no bullet is marked. Microsoft Learn ("Onboard a customer to
Azure Lighthouse", Troubleshooting) says "The `managedbyTenantId` value must not be the same as the
tenant ID for the subscription being onboarded", so in the walk's own subscriptions no delegation
names this tenant as its managing tenant, and a mark could never fire; its text would be false if
it did. The bundle README, the export help, the prompt, README.md, the about topic and
`docs/inventory-to-llm/README.md` now say that every row is access another tenant holds over a
subscription or resource group of this tenant. The rows of the mutation tables below that test the
mark (three "Final fix wave" rows of the `Get-OERInventoryReadme` table) and the README handed the
export's tenant (one of the `Export-OERInventory` table) record guards that BL-150 removed together
with their tests; they stay as the record of step 6b.

**Known limits.**

- (a) A delegation at a resource group whose definition an assignment of the subscription list also
  references -- the same offer delegated at the subscription and at a resource group -- is found
  only if the subscription list returns resource group assignments, since the fallback fires only for
  a definition no assignment of that list references (R-2). Learn does not say, and it was not
  measured.
- (b) No real delegation was measured: the test tenant holds none. The row shape, the expanded
  definition and the paging rest on Learn's documented fields and on mocked answers. A live check
  in a tenant that holds a delegation (the sprint's C-check P-15) would close it.
- (c) For a scope below a subscription, an assignment at a resource group the scope does not name,
  whose definition is neither expanded nor listed, makes the whole subscription unread, although its
  row would have been dropped by the keep filter anyway: the reader throws before that filter. Rare,
  since the list is read with `$expandRegistrationDefinition=true`.
- (d) A `-Scope` at a management group reads no delegation and names nothing (R-9): `-Scope` does
  not walk the subscriptions below it, and `-ManagementGroup` does.
- (e) `Export-OERInventory` recognises a failed subscription listing by the literal
  `<subscriptions: the listing failed>`, which `Resolve-OERInventoryScopeTree` writes. Closed in the
  final fix wave: the export test "recognises the subscription listing failure by the literal the
  REAL scope tree writes" runs the real tree with the subscription listing failing, so a change to
  the literal on either side turns it red (mutation proofs below).
- (f) The bundle README's Files bullet said the delegations are at the subscriptions in
  `scopeHierarchy.json`, which a `-Scope` run leaves without a subscription. Since the final fix
  wave it says "at the subscriptions the Azure walk visits", and the "None." text adds that a
  `-Scope` at a management group or the root scope visits no subscription, so it reads no
  delegation. The `azurePimEligibility.json` bullet beside it still names `scopeHierarchy.json` and
  stays loose there.
- (g) The reads from a managing tenant against a delegated customer subscription are not measured:
  no tenant here manages another (R-12). A refused read there names the subscription unread, as the
  role assignment walk already skips such a scope. If the read answers, it may also return that
  customer's delegations to a third managing tenant; such a row carries no mark, although it is
  neither access over this tenant nor access this tenant holds. Not measured either.

  *What BL-150 changed.* The export no longer makes these reads: since Sprint 11 step 6c the walk
  does not enter a subscription whose home tenant is another tenant, so neither the read against a
  delegated customer subscription nor a row of that customer's delegations to a third tenant can
  reach `lighthouseDelegations.json`. Such a subscription is named in the bundle README section
  "Subscriptions delegated from another tenant (not read)" instead, with one warning. What stays
  unmeasured is whether a managing tenant's subscription list reports a delegated customer
  subscription with the customer's `tenantId`, on which that selection rests
  ([#home-tenant-subscriptions](#home-tenant-subscriptions), R-1).

**Mutation proofs.** Each mutation was applied to the source, the module built, the covering tests
run and seen red, and the file restored, with `git status` clean after each; "N red" is the number of
failed tests in that run. Tasks 1 and 2 of the step ran them, and the final fix wave the rows marked
so; each row names the guard, the mutation, the first test that went red and the outcome.

**Equivalent mutants, each run and found green, and kept.**

- The reader's null filter over the definition list: a null entry has no id, so the blank id check
  after it skips it; only the blank id check is observable, and it is proved above.
- The reader's blank check on a referenced definition id: the set of references is asked only about
  keys of the definition index, which never holds a blank key.
- The blank half of the reader's lookup of a named definition: `ContainsKey('')` is false anyway,
  since the index holds no blank key.
- The null and blank guards of the reader's two role loops: the converter never yields a null
  authorization, and a blank role id gives an empty last segment that `Test-OERGuid` refuses (first
  loop) or that is no key of the role names (second loop).
- The converter's `[string[]]` cast of `delegatedRoleDefinitionIds`: an empty `object[]` serializes
  as `[]` too, and a one-element one stays an array. The Task 1 reports disagreed on whether this
  mutant was run, so the final fix wave ran it: the cast removed, the module built, the converter
  and reader suites green (49 passed, 0 failed), the file restored.
- `Export-OERInventory`'s `if ($null -ne $LighthouseRead)` (R-11): the module sets no StrictMode, so
  `$null.Unread` is `$null`, and `@($null)` is one null element, which the blank check right below
  drops; the path of a reader that returned nothing is behaviour-tested.
- `Export-OERInventory`'s `if ($null -ne $LighthouseCause)` (R-11): `Format-OERUnreadCauseClause`
  skips a null cause, and the list is read nowhere else.
- Not mutated, since it cannot differ: `-ceq` against `-eq` on the fixed literal
  `<subscriptions: the listing failed>`.

## home-tenant-subscriptions

Sprint 11 step 6c (BL-150, decision A19) kept `Export-OERInventory`'s Azure walk and
`Invoke-OERStructure`'s Azure sections in the subscriptions of the session's own tenant. This anchor
records the problem, the measurement, the decision, how it works, the rulings with what each costs if
it is wrong, the known limits and the mutation proofs. `Get-OERSubscriptionHomeTenant` is the single
owner of the decision (CLAUDE.md, Code Style), and gate 10 of `tests/QA/sourcehygiene.tests.ps1`
holds it to its callers ([#static-source-gates](#static-source-gates)): two in step 6c, three since
Sprint 11 step 8. One ErrorId was added,
`SubscriptionTenantMismatch` (category `InvalidOperation`); no public parameter, no document key and
no property of a public output object was added, and no public cmdlet other than `Export-OERInventory`
and `Invoke-OERStructure` changed in behaviour (the help of `Get-OERInventory` changed too). Sprint 11
step 8 (decision A20, BL-152) made `Get-OERInventory` the third caller and superseded R-11 and known
limit (c) for it; its part, "Sprint 11 step 8: Get-OERInventory checks too", closes this anchor.

**The problem (BL-150).** Sprint 11 step 6b's whole-branch review found that a managing (service
provider) tenant's subscription list also returns the customer subscriptions delegated to it through
Azure Lighthouse (inferred from Microsoft Learn, "Cross-tenant management experiences"; not measured),
and that the export's walk then entered them: role assignments, role management policies, PIM
eligibilities and Lighthouse rows of another tenant's subscription reached this tenant's bundle, and
a document or a proposal made from that bundle could make `Invoke-OERStructure` write, and under
`-Prune` remove, role assignments in the customer's subscription. Step 6b fixed only the texts and
marked a delegation this tenant manages in the bundle README
([#lighthouse-delegations](#lighthouse-delegations), R-12); carrying each subscription's tenant
through the scope tree and skipping the foreign ones was left to a later step. This is that step.

**The measurement (2026-10-15, live, reads only, as `oer-live-cc`).** No tenant or subscription value
is recorded here.

- M.0: the session's `TokenTenantId` is a GUID, the test tenant, and `ArmTokenTenantId` equals it.
- M.1: Subscriptions - List (api-version `2022-12-01`) answers `200` with one subscription, whose keys
  are `authorizationSource`, `displayName`, `id`, `managedByTenants`, `state`, `subscriptionId`,
  `subscriptionPolicies` and `tenantId`. `tenantId` is a GUID equal to `TokenTenantId`; there is no
  `homeTenantId` field in the REST answer; `managedByTenants` is `[]`.
- M.2: Subscriptions - Get of the test subscription answers the same keys and values.
- M.3: Subscriptions - Get of a made-up subscription id answers `404` `SubscriptionNotFound`; M.4: a
  role assignment read with `atScope()` at that subscription answers `404` `SubscriptionNotFound`
  too.
- M.5: `Get-OERSubscription` returns a `TenantId` equal to `TokenTenantId`.
- In all: 5 requests, 0 writes, 0 token calls after the sign-in; the leak check found nothing.

Microsoft Learn ("Onboard a customer to Azure Lighthouse", Troubleshooting) adds: "The
`managedbyTenantId` value must not be the same as the tenant ID for the subscription being
onboarded." So in the tenant's own subscriptions no delegation names this tenant as its managing
tenant.

**The decision (A19).** The export's Azure walk never enters a subscription whose home tenant is not
the session's tenant (`TokenTenantId`). Such a subscription is named in the bundle README as delegated
from another tenant, with ONE warning, and is not read -- no role assignments, policies, eligibility
or Lighthouse rows from it; that is a deliberate selection, not an unread collection. A subscription
whose home tenant cannot be decided (the field is missing or the read fails) is unread: named in
`IncompleteReads`, the export partial, nothing from it written. `Invoke-OERStructure` never writes,
and never prunes, a role assignment or role management policy at a scope in a subscription whose home
tenant is not the session's; the check is made once per subscription and run, before the first write
or read for a scope there; the row is `Failed` with ONE new ErrorId for the refusal, and nothing is
written. When the home tenant cannot be decided the row is `Failed` with the error as itself. The
public cmdlets (`New-OERRoleAssignment`, `Remove-OERRoleAssignment` and the rest, `Get-OERInventory`
included) do NOT change. (Superseded for `Get-OERInventory` alone by A20 in Sprint 11 step 8; see the
last part of this anchor. The other public cmdlets are still unchanged.)

**How it works.**

- **The owner.** `Get-OERSubscriptionHomeTenant` returns one object (`Scope`, `SubscriptionId`,
  `DisplayName`, `Verdict`, `HomeTenantId`, `SessionTenantId`, `Reason`, `ErrorRecord`) with one of
  four verdicts: `NoSubscription` (a management group or the root scope `/`; nothing is read),
  `Home`, `Foreign`, or `Undecided` (the scope breaks a spelling rule, the scope could not be
  resolved, the read failed, the subscription gave no `tenantId` that is a GUID, or the session holds
  no Graph token whose tenant ID is a GUID). The session's tenant is read through
  `Get-OERInventoryTenantId`, and the two are compared with `-eq` only when both pass `Test-OERGuid`.
  `-Subscription` decides a listed subscription from the `TenantId` the list returned, with no
  request. `-Scope` takes a scope in the document's syntax: an `mg:` form is `NoSubscription` with no
  resolution; any other form for which `Get-OERScopeSpellingProblem` returns a problem (only a stray
  `/` for a `sub:` or `subscription:` form) is `Undecided` with a `SubscriptionTenantMismatch` record
  that names the rules, and nothing is resolved or read for it (R-27); any other form is resolved
  by `Resolve-OERScope` (a subscription display name costs the subscription list) and made canonical;
  a scope inside `/subscriptions/{id}` costs one GET of the subscription (none without a session
  tenant). `-Cache` keeps what one read gave, a failed read included, under the lower-cased
  subscription id. A `Foreign` or `Undecided` verdict carries a `Reason` and an `ErrorRecord`: the
  resolver's or the read's own record, or a new `SubscriptionTenantMismatch` record (target the scope
  as given) when nothing failed. The owner never throws for a scope it cannot decide and never writes
  an error record; both catches scrub the record first.
- **The tree.** `Resolve-OERInventoryScopeTree` decides every listed subscription with
  `-Subscription` and walks only a `Home` one: a `Foreign` one goes to `ForeignSubscriptions`, an
  `Undecided` one to `UndecidedSubscriptions`, and neither reaches `Scopes` or the hierarchy. A
  `-Scope` costs one owner call: kept verbatim when `NoSubscription` or `Home`, and otherwise named in
  one of the two lists with the scope as given, `Scopes` then empty. The tree writes one warning per
  call naming every undecided subscription with its reason; the foreign ones it leaves to the caller.
- **The export.** `Export-OERInventory` writes ONE warning that names the foreign subscriptions,
  after the Lighthouse warning and before the bundle's `ShouldProcess`, so `-WhatIf` shows it and a
  Stop warning preference stops the export before the bundle is written. The README lists them in a
  section "Subscriptions delegated from another tenant (not read)", directly after the Lighthouse
  section. A foreign subscription alone makes no bundle partial. An undecided one is named in
  `IncompleteReads` as `subscriptionHomeTenant at <scope>`, after the role selection entries and
  before the Lighthouse ones, in the README under the label "Azure subscription whose tenant could not
  be read", and in a clause of the `InventoryPartial` message with its causes
  (`Format-OERUnreadCauseClause`). Of the subscriptions, `ScopesEnumerated` counts only the ones
  walked. The 6b
  README mark is removed ([#lighthouse-delegations](#lighthouse-delegations), R-12).
- **The engine.** `Invoke-OERStructure` keeps one cache per document. A `roleAssignments` entry is
  checked after its scope was resolved by the pre-pass (an entry whose scope could not be resolved
  still takes the existing branch first), with the resolved scope. A `roleManagementPolicies` entry
  is checked with its document scope, and an entry the check lets through is applied at the scope the
  check resolved (`Sync-OERStructureRoleManagementPolicy -ResolvedScope`, private), so the policy read
  and written is the one the check decided on; an `mg:` entry is resolved by the handler as before. A
  `Foreign` or `Undecided` verdict publishes the verdict's record once and adds one `Failed` row (the
  entry's label, and the Detail of the owner's `Reason`, its closing period dropped, followed by a
  fixed sentence), and the entry is never dispatched: no principal or role lookup, no read at the
  scope, no write. Every entry at one scope shares the verdict of its subscription, so a refused
  scope's prune pass never runs. No `ShouldProcess` is involved, so `-WhatIf` and a real run report
  the same row and send the same read of the subscription. A management group or the root scope
  costs no subscription read.
- **The gate.** Gate 10's owner table holds the row `Get-OERSubscriptionHomeTenant` with the owners
  `Resolve-OERInventoryScopeTree.ps1` and `Invoke-OERStructure.ps1`; its own `It` asserts the call
  count first, so a deleted row turns it red, and the whole-table floor rose to fourteen rows
  ([#static-source-gates](#static-source-gates)). Sprint 11 step 8 added `Get-OERInventory.ps1` as a
  third owner of the same row; the row count, and so the floor, did not change.

**Rulings.** Each with what it costs if it is wrong.

- **R-1 (the field).** A subscription's home tenant is ARM's subscription `tenantId` (Subscriptions -
  Get and List, `2022-12-01`, documented as "The subscription tenant ID"; Az PowerShell's
  `HomeTenantId` and the Azure CLI's `homeTenantId` map to it; the REST answer has no `homeTenantId`,
  measured), compared without regard to letter case with `TokenTenantId`, both canonical GUIDs.
  `managedByTenants` is not consulted: it names the managing tenants, and Learn's own list example
  shows per-subscription `tenantId` values that differ while `managedByTenants` lists the managers.
  If wrong (a managing tenant's list reports the managing tenant as the `tenantId` of a delegated
  subscription), the walk would read such a subscription as its own; the sprint's C-check P-15 in a
  managing tenant settles it, and the extra signal would be "the session tenant is listed in
  `managedByTenants`", one condition in the owner.
- **R-2 (one owner).** One private owner decides for the tree and the engine and reads the session's
  tenant through `Get-OERInventoryTenantId`: one rule, one place. If wrong, a second helper.
- **R-3 (no session tenant).** With no state, or a `TokenTenantId` that is not a GUID, every
  subscription is `Undecided` and nothing is read: the safer direction, since a tenant cannot be
  shown. If wrong, such a session exports no Azure subscription and applies no Azure entry in a
  subscription until its token names a tenant ID.
- **R-4 (a failed read is cached).** The read of a subscription is cached per run with its failure:
  "one check per subscription and run". If wrong, one transient failure fails every entry of that
  subscription in the run; re-run the document.
- **R-5 (a cache per document).** The engine's cache is per document, so a second piped document
  checks again, since the session may change between documents. If wrong, one extra GET per
  subscription per piped document.
- **R-6 (one ErrorId).** `SubscriptionTenantMismatch` (`InvalidOperation`) is the one new ErrorId
  (A9): for a foreign subscription, and for an undecided one where nothing failed (no `tenantId`, no
  session tenant, or a scope a document could not declare, R-27), as `DocumentTenantMismatch` covers
  "cannot be compared"; a failed read or a failed scope resolution is published as itself (A19). If
  wrong, a second ErrorId for "cannot be decided".
- **R-7 (where an undecided subscription is named).** In `IncompleteReads` as
  `subscriptionHomeTenant at <scope>`, after the role selection entries and before the Lighthouse
  entries (which stay last), with its own `InventoryPartial` clause and causes and one warning from
  the tree; not in `SkippedScopes` or `SkippedEligibilityScopes` (the specification says
  `IncompleteReads`; one name per gap). If wrong, two more list appends.
- **R-8 (the hierarchy).** Foreign and undecided subscriptions are left out of `scopeHierarchy.json`
  and `ScopesEnumerated`: the hierarchy describes this tenant's tree, and a customer's subscription
  name stays out of this tenant's bundle files except the README section. If wrong, one filter in the
  tree.
- **R-9 (the 6b mark is removed).** The README mark of step 6b (its R-12) and
  `Get-OERInventoryReadme -TenantId` are removed: Learn says a delegation's `managedByTenantId` must
  not be the subscription's own tenant, and the walk now reads only own subscriptions, so the mark can
  never fire and its text would be false if it did. If wrong, one parameter and one branch come back.
- **R-10 (the engine resolves a policy scope), as amended by R-17.** The engine resolves a
  `roleManagementPolicies` scope through the owner (a subscription display name costs the
  subscription list) and hands the handler the resolved scope (`-ResolvedScope`, private), so the
  policy read and written is the one the check decided on. A policy scope that cannot be resolved is
  now `Failed` by the engine with the resolver's record as itself, where the handler's
  `Get-OERRoleManagementPolicy` used to publish `InvalidScope`. No ErrorId is added, removed or
  renamed by this, but the ErrorId published for that case changed (R-17). If wrong, the engine wraps
  the resolver's record as `InvalidScope` (one constructor); raised to the architect.
- **R-11 (the public cmdlets are unchanged), as narrowed by R-24.** `Get-OERInventory` and every other
  public cmdlet are unchanged (A19): `Get-OERInventory` reads a scope it is given even in another
  tenant's subscription, and the apply refuses such a document's role assignment and policy rows in
  that subscription; a row it carries at a management group above that subscription, read as
  inherited, lies in no subscription, is not checked, and is applied like any management group row in
  the session's tenant (limit (c)). If wrong, `Get-OERInventory` gets the owner (one GET per call) in a
  later step. **Superseded for `Get-OERInventory` by A20 in Sprint 11 step 8**, which did exactly that
  (see the last part of this anchor); every other public cmdlet is still unchanged.
- **R-12 (CLAUDE.md).** CLAUDE.md gets the single-owner bullet and the gate-10 sentence, since it
  carries every owner rule, although the specification's list of texts does not name it. If wrong,
  one bullet comes out.
- **R-16 (the message names its commands).** The plan's `SubscriptionTenantMismatch` message said
  the whole module reads and writes only in a subscription it can show to belong to the session's
  tenant, which A19 contradicts (the public cmdlets are unchanged). The message names
  `Invoke-OERStructure` and `Export-OERInventory` instead. Its first form here said that both "read
  and write a role assignment or a role management policy only in a subscription they can show to
  belong to" the session's tenant; the final whole-branch review reworded it (M-1), since the engine
  also reads and writes at a management group, which lies in no subscription, and the export writes
  no role assignment. It now reads: "... Invoke-OERStructure reads and writes, and
  Export-OERInventory reads, a role assignment or a role management policy in a subscription only
  when they can show that the subscription belongs to the tenant the session's Microsoft Graph token
  was issued for -- not in one another tenant delegated to it, ...". The engine's refusal Detail
  ("the apply engine reads and writes a role assignment or a role management policy in a subscription
  only when it can show that the subscription belongs to this session's tenant, ...") was reworded the
  same way. The specification outranks the plan's wording, and the 6b final review caught the same
  kind of overclaim. If wrong, one sentence of the message again. Sprint 11 step 8 (A20) named the
  third command: "... Invoke-OERStructure reads and writes, and Export-OERInventory and
  Get-OERInventory read, a role assignment or a role management policy in a subscription only when
  they can show ...", the rest unchanged.
- **R-17 (a policy scope that cannot be resolved).** The step's own decision, not a stop: A19 says a
  row whose home tenant cannot be decided is `Failed` with the error as itself, and a resolver's
  failure is reported as itself, so a `roleManagementPolicies` scope that cannot be resolved (and any
  Azure entry whose subscription read fails) is `Failed` before the handler runs, with that record,
  in a plan and in a run alike. At the base of the step (`cd7e6a3`) such a policy entry behaved
  otherwise, as the Task 2 review measured: in a run it was `Failed` "failed to update role
  management policy", and `Invoke-OERStructure` published `InvalidScope` after two reads of the
  subscription list; under `-WhatIf` it was `Skipped` "would update ...". Now it costs one read of the
  list, and the published ErrorId is the resolver's: `AmbiguousName` for a display name two
  subscriptions share, or, for a name nobody carries, the resolver's plain message, which a thrown
  string makes its own id. This is recorded here and in the pull request, not in the release note,
  whose budget gives the step about 200 characters. If wrong, one sentence in `[Unreleased]` when a
  later step rewrites the section.
- **R-18 (an identity with a resource group role only).** Such an identity may be refused
  Subscriptions - Get; under A19 its role assignment and policy entries would then be `Failed` with
  that refusal as itself, and an export `-Scope` by it would be unread (partial). It cannot be
  measured here without changing an identity's roles, so it is a known limit (below), a question for
  the operator in the sprint's C-check P-15, and a finding; raised to the architect. If wrong (such
  an identity is refused), an operator whose roles cover only resource groups loses the apply of
  Azure entries until the owner learns another signal.
- **R-19 (the refusal's shape).** The engine refuses a verdict that is `Foreign` or `Undecided`, as
  the plan wrote it; the owner returns exactly four verdicts, pinned by its own tests. If wrong, a
  fifth verdict added later passes the engine unchecked until the change that adds it to the owner
  adds it here too.
- **R-20 (no test of the owner inside a latched command).** The owner's GET goes through
  `Invoke-OERArmRequest`, whose latch gate the transport suites and gate 10 hold, so no test runs the
  real owner inside a command whose sign-in was refused. If wrong, a refused command's Azure entries
  fail with `SignInRefused` (the Task 2 implementer saw exactly that in two transport scenarios)
  without a test pinning it.
- **R-24 (a management group row read through another tenant's subscription).** R-11 leaves a gap
  open, and this ruling keeps it open in this step. `Get-OERRoleAssignment` without a filter returns
  the assignments that apply at a scope, inherited ones included, and `Get-OERInventory` leaves out
  only the root scope and the scopes no document can declare, so a document `Get-OERInventory` made at
  a subscription of another tenant can carry role assignment rows at management groups above that
  subscription. Such a row lies in no subscription: the owner rates it `NoSubscription`, and the
  engine dispatches it like any management group row. Its principal is an object of the customer's
  tenant, which the directory of the session's tenant does not return, so `Get-OERInventory` writes
  it by its object id with `principalStatus` (when that lookup was read; a lookup that failed is named
  unread instead), and the engine never creates such an entry (`Sync-OERStructureRoleAssignment`,
  step 5a: `Skipped`, with no `ShouldProcess`). The prune pass at that scope still runs under
  `-Prune`, so the realistic effect is the prune half: if the session's tenant holds a management
  group of that id, the role assignments defined there that the document does not declare are
  removed, unless an entry at that scope whose role or principal cannot be resolved there withholds
  the prune. Which management group Azure Resource Manager reaches under the session's token is not
  measured. If wrong (the step should close it), the engine also refuses a management group row whose
  name is not in the session tenant's hierarchy: a new check the architect decides (R-28). Since
  Sprint 11 step 8 (A20) `Get-OERInventory` writes no row at all for a `-Scope` or `-Subscription` in a
  subscription of another tenant, inherited management group rows included, so a document it makes
  can no longer carry this path; a document written another way still can, and the engine check
  R-28 suggests was not added.
- **R-26 (an export -Scope that cannot be resolved).** An export `-Scope` the resolver cannot resolve
  is named `subscriptionHomeTenant at <scope as given>` in `IncompleteReads` and no longer in
  `SkippedScopes`/`SkippedEligibilityScopes`, and the Lighthouse reader is not asked about it -- A19:
  a scope whose subscription cannot be told is unread and named in `IncompleteReads`, one name per gap
  (R-7); the export is partial either way. If wrong, the `-Scope` goes back to `SkippedScopes` in a
  later step.
- **R-27 (a scope a document could not declare).** A raw `-Scope` (one starting with `/`) for which
  `Get-OERScopeSpellingProblem` returns any problem is `Undecided` with a `SubscriptionTenantMismatch`
  record naming the problem, and nothing is resolved or read -- the ARM transport's `System.Uri`
  turns `.`, `..`, `%2e` and `\` into another path than the text the owner decided on, and the
  spelling owner already refuses exactly these spellings in a document, so the owner decides only on
  text that is the path sent. If wrong, an export `-Scope` with a spelling a document could not
  declare (a trailing `/`, for example), which was read before, is now unread (partial) until written
  without it. The check stands after the owner's `mg:` early return and before the resolution; for a
  `sub:` or `subscription:` form the spelling owner reports only a stray `/`, which makes that form
  `Undecided` the same way. The engine is not affected, since the validator refuses these spellings
  in a document first; the final whole-branch review found the gap in the export (an export `-Scope`
  of `/subscriptions/<own>/../../subscriptions/<foreign>` was rated `Home` on the own subscription's
  read and then read at the foreign one, and a management group path with `..` segments was rated
  `NoSubscription` with no read).
- **R-28 (the R-24 path stays open).** The R-24 `-Prune` path is an old path the step does not
  worsen (it closed the same document's subscription half); it is reported to the architect with a
  suggested follow-up: refuse a management group row whose id is not in the session tenant's
  hierarchy, or keep `Get-OERInventory`'s inherited rows above its scope out of the document.
- **R-29 (an export at the root scope).** A known limit, (h) below: a `/` `-Scope` export reads at the
  root scope with no `atScope()` filter, as before; whether Azure Resource Manager returns rows of
  delegated subscriptions there is not measured (it needs access at the root scope the test identity
  does not hold).

**Known limits.**

- (a) R-1 is not measured in a managing tenant: no tenant here manages another. That a managing
  tenant's subscription list reports a delegated customer subscription with the customer's
  `tenantId` rests on Learn; the sprint's C-check P-15 records it.
- (b) R-18 is not measured: whether an identity whose Azure role covers only a resource group is
  refused Subscriptions - Get. The live checklist of the step covers only an identity with no Azure
  role at all. If it is refused, such an identity's role assignment and policy entries are `Failed`
  with that refusal, and its export `-Scope` is unread.
- (c) **Superseded for `Get-OERInventory` by A20 in Sprint 11 step 8** (see the last part of this
  anchor): it now checks the subscription of a `-Scope` or `-Subscription` and writes no row in one of
  another tenant, so the document described below is no longer one it makes. The text below is the
  step 6c record, kept as written; it still holds for every other public cmdlet. The public cmdlets do
  not check (A19, R-11, R-24). `New-OERRoleAssignment`,
  `Set-OERRoleManagementPolicy`, `Get-OERInventory` and the rest use the scope they are given, so a
  write through them still reaches a delegated subscription. A document `Get-OERInventory` made at
  such a subscription is refused row by row when it is applied, but only for its rows in that
  subscription. Its role assignments are read with no filter, which returns the inherited ones too,
  and only the root scope and the scopes no document can declare are left out, so it can also carry
  rows at management groups above that subscription. Such a row lies in no subscription, and the
  engine does not check it. Its principal is an object of the customer's tenant, which the session
  tenant's directory does not return, so `Get-OERInventory` writes it with `principalStatus` (when the
  lookup was read) and the engine never creates it; but under `-Prune` the engine still prunes at
  that scope, so if the session's tenant holds a management group of that id, the role assignments
  defined there that the document does not declare are removed (unless an entry there whose role or
  principal cannot be resolved withholds the prune). Which management group Azure Resource Manager
  reaches is not measured (R-24, R-28).
- (d) A session whose token names no GUID tenant exports no subscription and applies no
  `roleAssignments` or `roleManagementPolicies` entry in a subscription (R-3).
- (e) A failed subscription read is cached for the document (R-4), so one transient failure fails
  every entry in that subscription until the document is applied again.
- (f) An export `-Scope` that `Resolve-OERScope` cannot resolve -- for example a raw scope that does
  not start with `/`; a `sub:` name nobody carries, or one two subscriptions share, is named the same
  way -- is now named `subscriptionHomeTenant at <scope>`, with the resolver's message in its cause,
  and makes the bundle partial; before the step it reached `Get-OERInventory` and was skipped, which
  made the bundle partial too (R-26). So is an export `-Scope` with a spelling no document can declare
  (R-27): nothing is resolved or read for it, and its cause names the rules it breaks; one written with
  a trailing `/` was read before the step. Such a scope need not lie in a subscription at all -- a
  management group path with a stray `/` is refused the same way -- yet the tree's warning, the
  `InventoryPartial` clause and the README label still call it a subscription whose tenant could not be
  read. The export help names both cases among the causes.
- (g) The engine's two owner calls stand outside the per-entry `try`, where the plan placed them. An
  owner that threw would end the document instead of failing one row; it cannot throw for any scope
  the validator admits, since every resolution and read sits in the owner's own `try`.
- (h) A `/` `-Scope` export reads at the root scope with no `atScope()` filter, as before (R-29);
  whether Azure Resource Manager returns rows of delegated subscriptions there is not measured (it
  needs access at the root scope the test identity does not hold).

**Mutation proofs.** Each mutation was made in a copy of `source/` in a scratch folder and run with
the dev-mode test harness against the named test files, never in the worktree; a gate mutation ran
the copied gate in a scratch project root. "N red" is the number of failed tests in that run. Every
mutant turned at least one test red; for two of them, M8 and M6, one case is equivalent, which no test
can tell apart (see below the second table).

Task 1 (the owner, the tree, the README and the export; lines at `637c4ba`, M30 at `fe6e64c`, and
the rows F1a, F1b, F6a and F6b of the final fix wave at `89d9c35`).
Prefixes: HT is the Describe `Get-OERSubscriptionHomeTenant (BL-150, A19)`, TR is
`Resolve-OERInventoryScopeTree`'s Describe "only the home tenant's subscriptions are walked", EX is
`Export-OERInventory stays in the home tenant's subscriptions (BL-150, A19)` and RM is
`Get-OERInventoryReadme (subscriptions delegated from another tenant, BL-150, A19)`; ST, in the F
rows, is the engine's Describe named under the second table.

### Sprint 11 step 8: Get-OERInventory checks too (A20, BL-152)

**The problem (BL-152).** R-11 and known limit (c) left `Get-OERInventory` reading any scope it was
given. A standalone `Get-OERInventory -Scope` or `-Subscription` in a subscription another tenant
delegated to this one read that subscription's role assignments and role management policies into a
document, inherited rows at management groups above it included (the R-24 path), and only the
engine's row-by-row refusal stood between that document and a write.

**The decision (A20).** `Get-OERInventory` becomes the third caller of the owner, with the rule the
walk and the engine keep: its `RoleAssignments` and `RoleManagementPolicies` sections read a `-Scope`
or a `-Subscription` only in a subscription of the session's tenant. No public parameter, no ErrorId
and no output property was added; the other public cmdlets are unchanged.

**How it works.**

- **The check.** A local function of `Get-OERInventory` asks the owner, for each of `-Scope` and
  `-Subscription` (as `sub:<value>`) that is not blank, ONCE per invocation -- by the first of the two
  sections that asks -- after that section's own guards and before its reader runs; the second
  section reuses the verdicts. `-ManagementGroup` is never checked: a management group scope lies in
  no subscription, so there is no subscription home tenant to compare, and the owner rates a
  management group or the root scope `NoSubscription` anyway. Which management group Azure Resource
  Manager reaches under the session's token, the session tenant's own or another's, is not measured:
  that is the residual risk R-24 describes, and this check does not close it.
- **Foreign.** Any `Foreign` verdict refuses both sections: nothing is read there and no row is
  written. The owner's `SubscriptionTenantMismatch` record is written ONCE per invocation, after the
  inventory object (the place `InventoryPartial` takes), and the sections are not reported unread:
  a refusal is not a failed read. With both `-Scope` and `-Subscription` in subscriptions of another
  tenant, only the first verdict's record is written, the `-Scope`'s.
- **Undecided.** With no `Foreign` verdict, any verdict other than `Home` or `NoSubscription` refuses
  the sections too, and each included section is named unread by its own name (`roleAssignments`,
  `roleManagementPolicies`) with the verdict's `Reason` as the cause (its trailing period trimmed),
  so `InventoryPartial` names it; its record is not written separately.
- **The ARM token.** The check reads the subscription through the ARM transport, which sends nothing
  without an ARM token, and the readers used to acquire the token on first use, after the check. So
  `begin` asks for it in the command's one `Initialize-OERAuth` call, as `-IncludeARM` does, whenever
  `RoleAssignments`, or `RoleManagementPolicies` with exactly one of `-Role`, `-CommonRoles` and
  `-AllRolesAtScope`, is included with a `-Scope` or a `-Subscription` that is not blank;
  `-ManagementGroup` alone keeps the readers' acquisition on first use, and a call that includes
  neither section asks for none. `RoleManagementPolicies` with none or more than one of the three is
  skipped with a warning before the check and reads nothing, so since the step's final fix round it
  asks for no token (before it, it did, and a failed ARM sign-in then latched the call's Entra ID
  sections for a section that read nothing); `begin` computes the one `$RoleSources` list that
  section decides by, so the two conditions cannot drift apart.
- **No extra request inside an export.** The run context gets one member, `SubscriptionTenant`
  ([#export-run-context](#export-run-context)). The export hands it to `Resolve-OERInventoryScopeTree
  -Cache`, which hands it to both of its owner calls; the owner's `-Cache` now also belongs to the
  `-Subscription` set and stores there what the list gave for each listed subscription, with no
  request. `Get-OERInventory` uses the member while the context is in force and holds it, and a cache
  of its own otherwise, so its per-scope calls inside an export are answered from what the walk
  already decided.
- **The gate.** Gate 10's `Get-OERSubscriptionHomeTenant` row names `Get-OERInventory.ps1` as its third
  owner ([#static-source-gates](#static-source-gates)).

**The measurement (mocked, with the real tree, owner, `Get-OERInventory` and readers inside the
export).** The ARM requests the same exports sent before the step were measured with the same test on
the unchanged build and pinned: a listed walk of one management group and one own subscription, both
sections with `-AllRolePolicies`, sends no subscription GET and four ARM requests (the role
assignments and the policy assignments at each scope), and an export `-Scope` at a resource group sends the tree's one subscription GET and then the
two lists at the resource group, three in all -- the same requests as before the step. A standalone
call costs one subscription GET (and the subscription list for a `-Subscription` named by display
name) before its readers; the rows it writes for the session's own subscription are the rows it wrote
before, measured on a dev-mode import of the code before the check.

**Rulings of the step.** Each with what it costs if it is wrong. (The step's own numbering; they are
not the R-numbers of step 6c above.)

- **Step 8 R-2 (no new parameter).** "No new parameter" is read as no new public parameter and none on
  `Get-OERInventory`: the owner's existing `-Cache` joins the `-Subscription` set and the private tree
  gets an optional `-Cache`, so the answers reach `Get-OERInventory` through the run context's one new
  member. If wrong, the tree returns its verdict facts and the export fills the cache itself.
- **Step 8 R-6 (Foreign is a refusal, Undecided is unread).** A foreign subscription writes the owner's
  record once and is not unread; an undecided one writes no record of its own and is unread. If wrong,
  the undecided record (a read's own error) should be surfaced as itself too.
- **Step 8 R-9 (the ARM token at sign-in).** When the sign-in for that token fails
  (`ArmTokenAcquisitionFailed`), the whole command is latched and its Entra ID sections send nothing
  too, as with `-IncludeARM`, where before the step those sections were read and only the readers
  failed. If wrong, an operator whose ARM sign-in fails loses the Entra ID part of such a call.
- **Step 8 R-10 (one record).** With both scopes foreign only the `-Scope`'s record is written. If
  wrong, the second scope's reason is not printed (the readers refuse that combination anyway).

**What changed for a caller, beyond the refusal.** A standalone `-Scope` that does not start with `/`,
a `-Subscription` name nobody carries or two subscriptions share, and a `-Scope` in a spelling no
document can declare (R-27 of step 6c, a trailing `/` among them) are now `Undecided`: both sections
are written empty and named in `InventoryPartial` with the reason, where before the readers' own error
was written (or, for a trailing `/`, the scope was read). A session whose Graph token names no tenant
ID gets both sections unread the same way (R-3 of step 6c). Every standalone scoped call with
`RoleAssignments` or `RoleManagementPolicies` included reads the subscription once, before the first
of the two sections reads; a `RoleManagementPolicies` section skipped for its role parameters (none,
or more than one, of `-Role`, `-CommonRoles` and `-AllRolesAtScope`) reads nothing, the subscription
included.

**Known limits.** (a) With `-Scope` foreign and `-Subscription` undecided, the foreign verdict wins and
the undecided reason is not named. (b) Limit (b) of step 6c now reaches `Get-OERInventory` too: if an
identity whose Azure role covers only a resource group is refused Subscriptions - Get, its scoped
call is unread. (c) The other public cmdlets still use the scope they are given (limit (c) above).
(d) A `-Subscription` given by its display name is resolved by the owner for the check and again by
each reader for its read, so a name that moved to another subscription between the two resolutions
could be read unchecked (theoretical; not measured). A follow-up would pass the owner's resolved
scope to the readers; the step's final review left it as it is. Sprint 11 step 10 did exactly that
for `-Subscription` (BL-155, R-4), in the subsection below.

**Mutation proofs.** Each mutation was made in a copy of `source/` (a dev-mode module in scratch for
the fix round) and run against the named tests; every mutant turned at least one test red, and the

the decision is made once per invocation, so no cache and a cache of its own send the same one GET.

### Sprint 11 step 10: the readers are handed the subscription id the check resolved (BL-155, R-4)

**The problem (BL-155, fifth point).** Known limit (d) above. A `-Subscription` given by its display
name was resolved by the check (`Get-OERSubscriptionHomeTenant` through `Resolve-OERScope`, one read of
the subscription list) and then resolved again by `Get-OERRoleAssignment` and
`Get-OERRoleManagementPolicy`, each through the same list: two more list reads per call, and a second
decision about which subscription the name means, made after the check had shown one subscription to
be the session tenant's own. Display names are not unique, so a name that moved between the two
resolutions could have been read unchecked (theoretical; not measured).

**The decision (R-4).** With `-Subscription` given and the check's verdict `Home`, both readers get
`-Subscription` with the `SubscriptionId` of that verdict, a GUID that `Resolve-OERScope` takes as it is
with no list read, instead of the name. The check keeps the id in its holder the first time it decides.
A `-Subscription` verdict is `Undecided` unless the holder has an id: both sections are named unread by
their own names, the cause says the subscription check gave no subscription id for the scope as given, and
nothing is read by name. The rule is decided on the holder, which is set for a `Home` verdict that carries
an id and for nothing else, and not on the verdict's own id (fix round 1: the first commit tested the
verdict's id, so a `NoSubscription` answer WITH an id for `sub:` passed the filter and handed both readers
`-Subscription $null`). So a `Home` answer without an id, and a `NoSubscription` answer with or without
one, are all `Undecided`. The owner never answers `sub:` that way (its `Home` always carries the id of the
path it resolved, and it never answers `NoSubscription` for `sub:`), so the rule is a backstop. A `-Scope`
is unchanged: it goes to the readers as given and its `Home` verdict needs no id. No public parameter,
ErrorId or output property was added (A9). Cost if wrong: the two assignments go back to `$Subscription`
and the id-less rule goes, one line each.

**What changed for a caller.** A standalone `-Subscription` given by display name costs one read of the
subscription list, the check's, where it cost three (the check's and one in each reader); the requests
after the check name the subscription by id. The test that pins the requests through the real owner and
readers, 'asks for the token in the sign-in and reads a -Subscription given by its display name ...', lost
its two later list reads.

**The binding refusal (BL-155, second point).** `-Scope`, `-Subscription` and `-ManagementGroup` of
`Get-OERInventory`, and `-Scope` and `-ManagementGroup` of `Export-OERInventory`, refuse a value of white
space at binding, the BL-96 pattern of `-GroupFilter` (a `[ValidateScript()]` declared above
`[ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]`, since validation attributes run in reverse declaration order). Before it, a
value of spaces passed the sections' own truthiness tests and reached the readers, while the check and
the sign-in's ARM term (`IsNullOrWhiteSpace`) took it for no scope at all. No call inside the module
passes one a blank value: the export's per-scope calls hand `Get-OERInventory` a scope the tree listed,
which the tree adds only when it is not empty, and its Entra ID call passes no Azure parameter. No
parameter moved, so positional binding is unchanged.

**Mutation proofs.** Each mutation was made in the source of the step's Task 1 commit and run against the
named tests; every mutant turned at least one test red, and the restored source was green. Lines are the
commit's.

| M5a | an id-less `Home` for `-Subscription` is undecided, `:798` | the term made `$false` | 4 red |

| M5c | the cause of an id-less answer, `:806` | `NoSubscription` left out of the list | 1 red |
| V1, V2, V3 | the three white space refusals, `:481`, `:485`, `:489` | each `[ValidateScript()]` removed | 5, 4 and 4 red |
| V3b, V3c | the null or empty refusal and the order of the two attributes, `:482`, `:481` | `[ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]` removed; the two swapped | 2 red each |
| V4, V5, V5b | the same for the export, `Export-OERInventory.ps1:660`, `:657`, `:661` | each removed | 5, 4 and 2 red |
| O1, O2 | no parameter moved, `Get-OERInventory.ps1:491`, `Export-OERInventory.ps1:657` | `-Role` above `-ManagementGroup`; `-Scope` above `-ManagementGroup` | 7 and 1 red |

### CLAUDE.md text for home-tenant-subscriptions

What CLAUDE.md said about this rule before Sprint 11 step 11b cut it to the rule itself:

- **`Get-OERSubscriptionHomeTenant` is the single owner of whether a subscription's home tenant is
  the session's tenant (A19, BL-150)** -- ARM's subscription `tenantId` (Subscriptions - Get or List,
  api-version `2022-12-01`) against `Get-OERInventoryTenantId`, compared without regard to letter
  case and only when both are canonical GUIDs. It is called only by `Resolve-OERInventoryScopeTree`,
  `Invoke-OERStructure` and `Get-OERInventory` (gate 10), never by another public cmdlet: the role
  assignment and policy cmdlets use the scope they are given. `Get-OERInventory` (A20, BL-152) checks
  each of `-Scope` and `-Subscription` (as `sub:<value>`) that is given, ONCE per invocation, before
  the first read of RoleAssignments or RoleManagementPolicies; `-ManagementGroup` is never checked.
  That check reads through the ARM transport, so its `begin` asks for the ARM token in its one
  `Initialize-OERAuth` call, exactly as `-IncludeARM` does, whenever RoleAssignments, or
  RoleManagementPolicies with exactly one of `-Role`, `-CommonRoles` and `-AllRolesAtScope`
  (the rule that section reads by, from the one `$RoleSources` list), is included with a `-Scope` or
  `-Subscription` that is not blank (R-9); a `-ManagementGroup` alone keeps the readers'
  acquisition on first use, and a call with neither section asks for none. A
  foreign subscription is read for nothing -- each included section empty, the owner's
  `SubscriptionTenantMismatch` record written once (the first foreign verdict's), after the inventory,
  and not unread; an undecided
  one is read for nothing too, each included section named unread by its own name through
  `InventoryPartial`. Inside an export the answers are shared through the run context's
  `SubscriptionTenant`, which the tree fills (`-Cache`, the listed facts included), so the check sends
  no extra request. `Export-OERInventory`'s walk enters
  only a subscription of the session's tenant, names one of another tenant with one warning and in
  its README, and names one it cannot decide in `IncompleteReads` (partial). The engine checks once
  per subscription and document, before the first read or write of a `roleAssignments` or
  `roleManagementPolicies` scope there, and refuses the entry `Failed` with `SubscriptionTenantMismatch`
  -- or with the read's or the resolver's own record when that failed -- reading no role assignment or
  policy there, writing nothing and never pruning there. Never decide a subscription's tenant anywhere else.
  `Why: docs/development/rationale.md#home-tenant-subscriptions`
